Today our class is the {{< vocab "assembly" zh=true >}} of Athens. Like real Athenian {{< vocab "citizen" text="citizens" zh=true >}}, you will listen to speeches and then {{< vocab "vote" zh=true >}}.

## The question

> **Should our class have 10 minutes of free reading every day?**

## How it works

1. **Speeches.** Two speakers argue *for*, then two argue *against*. Each speaks for one minute.
2. **Questions.** Anyone may ask a speaker one question.
3. **Vote.** Raise your hand for *yes*, then for *no*. The teacher counts.
4. **Twist.** Your teacher may say only *some* students can vote this time, just like Athens.

## Tally

| | Vote 1: everyone | Vote 2: only "citizens" |
|---|---|---|
| **Yes** | | |
| **No** | | |
| **Result** | | |
: {tbl-colwidths="[24,38,38]"}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## {{< vocab "reflect" text="Reflect" zh=true >}} on the vote

**a.** Did the result change in Vote 2? {{< vocab "explain" text="Explain" zh=true >}} why.

{{< lines 2 >}}

**b.** Was it fair that only some people could vote in Athens? {{< vocab "explain" text="Explain" zh=true >}}.

{{< lines 2 >}}

**c.** {{< vocab "identify" text="Identify" zh=true >}} one way our class vote was like the real Assembly, and one way it was different:

{{< lines 2 >}}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.callout-note title="Teacher notes"}
For Vote 2, choose "citizens" by a rule students didn't pick (birthday month, or seats on one side of the room), then let only them vote. Most classes see the result flip. Use **b.** to connect to who was left out in Athens: women, enslaved people and foreigners.
:::
:::
